hypothesis: Default Medusa locking uses InMemoryLockingProvider, so the keyed lock wrapping reserveInventoryStep only serializes requests inside one server process. With two servers sharing one database, two carts each needing the single SOLO unit (stock 1) can both pass the availability check and both create reservations, giving an oversell. I expect no_oversell to fail on some runs when the completions are released together across servers 1 and 2.

schema: oversold.scenario/v1
name: solo-cross-server-race
description: Two carts each hold the single SOLO unit and are completed together, one on each server, to test whether the in-process lock lets both through.
target:
  engine: medusa
  version: 2.22.0
  servers: 2
stock:
  SOLO: 1
carts:
  alice:
    server: 1
    lines:
    - sku: OVS-SOLO
      qty: 1
  bob:
    server: 2
    lines:
    - sku: OVS-SOLO
      qty: 1
race:
- id: alice-completes
  server: 1
  do: complete
  cart: alice
- id: bob-completes
  server: 2
  do: complete
  cart: bob
timing:
  release: together
  jitter_ms:
  - 0
  - 3
faults: []
runs: 20
seed: 7

hypothesis: Within one cart, OVS-PIECE and OVS-TWOPACK both draw from the shared WIDGET item (stock 10). A cart with OVS-PIECE qty 6 and OVS-TWOPACK qty 3 needs 12 WIDGET units. If each line is checked against stock alone, each passes separately and the order over-reserves. I expect no_oversell to fail when a single cart with these lines is completed, or when two such carts race.
